title: View-count principle on Hackage (Haskell packages)

gate_results_50.overall: G1 PASS, G2 PASS, G3 conditional, G4 PASS

gate_results_100.overall: G1 PASS, G2 PASS, G3 conditional, G4 PASS

key_finding: Need-related Haskell packages have 2.90x higher mean download activity than random packages (mean 19,821 vs 6,844). Sample size dependence observed: ratio 1.11x (n=50) → 2.90x (n=100). All Gates G1-G4 pass on Hackage with tag-based classification (100% coverage). Effect size increases with sample size, suggesting the differentiation is robust.
boundary_condition: View-count principle generalizes to Haskell package ecosystem on Hackage; tag-based classification achievable with 100% coverage; sample-size-dependent effect observed; no candidate validated. Larger samples reveal stronger differentiation between need-related and random packages.
continuation_note: E133v3 (n=100) confirms and strengthens the effect. The sample-size dependence suggests the classification differentiates packages with significantly different download patterns. Next: E133v4 with even larger sample or different tag categories to further validate the effect.
